title: Fixed-edge triangle prism gives coherent precomposition
statement:
Use quasicategories, fixed-endpoint arrow spaces and left-pinch maps as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and [lem-coef-infinity-left-pinch-comparison], and the triangle mapping space and composition classes of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Work in a fixed containing universe. Let $p:\mathcal E\to\mathcal B$ be a simplicial functor of quasicategories, let $s:x\to y$ be an edge of $\mathcal E$, and let $z$ be a vertex. Define $T_{\mathcal E}(s,z)$ degreewise as the simplicial set of $(m+2)$-simplices whose first edge is $s$ and whose face on vertices $2,\ldots,m+2$ is constantly $z$, with operators induced by order maps on those last vertices fixing $0,1$; define $T_{\mathcal B}(p(s),p(z))$ similarly. Let $r_0:T_{\mathcal E}(s,z)\to L_{\mathcal E}(x,z)$ restrict to the face omitting vertex $1$, and let $r_1:T_{\mathcal E}(s,z)\to L_{\mathcal E}(y,z)$ restrict to the face omitting vertex $0$; use the same notation over $\mathcal B$. For every $m$-simplex $t:\Delta^{m+2}\to\mathcal E$ of $T_{\mathcal E}(s,z)$, precomposition with the map $\Delta^2\times\Delta^m\to\Delta^{m+2}$ induced by the monotone map $[2]\times[m]\to[m+2]$, $(0,i)\mapsto0$, $(1,i)\mapsto1$, $(2,i)\mapsto i+2$, gives an $m$-simplex $e(t)$ of the triangle space $V(x,y,z)$ of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]; this defines a simplicial map $e:T_{\mathcal E}(s,z)\to V(x,y,z)$. Its edge restrictions are $\theta\circ e=(j^Lr_1,c_s)$ and $\ell\circ e=j^Lr_0$, where $\theta,\ell$ are the restrictions of that node, $j^L$ the left-pinch maps of [lem-coef-infinity-left-pinch-comparison], and $c_s$ the constant map at the vertex $s$ of $U_{\mathcal E}(x,y)$. Consequently, in homotopy classes of maps $T_{\mathcal E}(s,z)\to U_{\mathcal E}(x,z)$,
$$[j^Lr_0]=[\ell]\,[\theta]^{-1}\bigl([j^Lr_1],[c_s]\bigr),$$
that is, the roof
$$U_{\mathcal E}(y,z)\xleftarrow{\ j^Lr_1\ }T_{\mathcal E}(s,z)\xrightarrow{\ j^Lr_0\ }U_{\mathcal E}(x,z)$$
represents precomposition by $s$ transported to the arrow spaces, and $e$ supplies its triangle witness. The same construction over $\mathcal B$ for $p(s)$ and $p(z)$ gives $e_{\mathcal B}$, and $p\circ e=e_{\mathcal B}\circ p$, $p\circ r_k=r_k\circ p$ $(k=0,1)$ and $p\circ j^L=j^L\circ p$ hold as equalities of simplicial maps; hence the two roofs, their triangle witnesses and the vertical maps induced by $p$ form a strictly commuting diagram, which presents the precomposition square for $s$ and $p(s)$ together with its commutation data.

source.place: Proposition 4.6.8.16 and its proof (the map e and the strictly commuting diagram), Remark 4.6.8.17, and Construction 4.6.8.9/Notation 4.6.8.15. Fixed-edge triangle-prism model of precomposition; strict naturality follows by applying the simplicial functor to these prescribed prisms. Read online 2026-10-17; no archived copy in literature/.
